title: CoRP recognition of polynomial identity
statement: A polynomial identity testing instance is a pair of nonempty, well-formed arithmetic circuits over the integers with the same number of input variables, whose computed polynomials are equal; encode the pair by doubling each bit of the first circuit code, appending the separator $01$, and then the second code. The language of such encodings belongs to coRP: there is a polynomial-time randomized verifier that always rejects an identity and accepts every string outside this language with probability at least $2/3$.
